scope: The implemented success coordinate agrees with the signed reciprocal on regular bins. The decoded phase distance bounds the relative error even across a sign change.

The exact sine clock on either spectral sign has squared relative error of order 1/(dM)² for any superposition. For a normalized input the selected branch has mass at least 4d² and normalized vector error at most 160/(dM), preserved by unitary uncomputation.

The sine-clock distribution is normalized and satisfies a circular second-moment bound independent of the eigenphase.

The inverse Fourier transform, controlled-time phases and sine-state preparation give the exact eigenphase kernel. Their adjoint uncomputes the reciprocal-weighted state to a zero clock. The signed solution branch has probability at least 4d² and normalized error at most 160/(dM).
The initialized sine-envelope clock has unit norm and is prepared by a unitary.
The controlled-time phases and quantum Fourier transform are unitary.
The direct sum of unitary eigenphase-clock blocks is unitary on the combined register.
The unitary composes the preparation, forward clock, signed reciprocal rotation and inverse clock. Its selected amplitudes and Born mass agree with the analyzed solution branch.

Unknown-success amplitude amplification of this signed solver succeeds with probability at least 1/8 averaged over the chosen depths. Its conditional solution is preserved up to global phase, and the solver and inverse calls are counted.
The fixed forward and adjoint clock words use controlled evolutions and return their work bit on arbitrary input clock states.

For 4d ≤ |λ| ≤ 1/4, the signed solver attains vector error ε and constant success with at most 2/d input-preparation or inverse calls and 640/(d²ε) exact controlled evolutions. Elementary sparse runtime requires additional synthesis.
The uniform forward and adjoint words query the evolution in the original Hermitian matrix basis. The eigenvector transformation is used to prove their action on every clock state.

For an invertible finite Hermitian matrix of either spectral sign in the stated bands, the clean-clock target is the ordinary inverse applied to the input in its original basis. At clock length M the normalized successful state has vector error at most 160/(dM) and unamplified probability at least 4d².
